rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, Tables 5-8, Figs 3-5 - the authors run their own SWAP model simulations for the San Giorgio East district (2010-2013), calibrate an empirical percolation-groundwater depth relationship against bi-weekly piezometer measurements (R2 0.86 calibration, 0.90 validation) and run scenario analyses of a shift from continuous submergence to flush irrigation.
rows.notes: The study concerns flush irrigation (intermittent surface flushing of non-submerged rice fields, 150 mm applications on demand), not drip irrigation; drip is never tested or simulated. What the study shows (Section 3.3, Table 7, Conclusions) is that a district-wide shift from continuous submergence to flush irrigation of rice reduces percolation/groundwater recharge, deepens summer groundwater (~35 cm), and raises simulated maize irrigation requirements by ~50% (750 to 1050 mm) because the 15-day turn becomes insufficient; the rice irrigation reduction falls from ~80% to ~60% when feedback is accounted for. These scenario outputs are model results not checked against observations of the modified system. The technology in the passage (drip) does not match, so Q2 is no.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a scenario modelling analysis for flush-irrigated rice in a shallow-groundwater district in Northern Italy; present-state groundwater depth relationship validated against piezometer data, but scenario results are unvalidated model outputs. Authors note results may differ in less permeable soils and that yield gaps, nutrient dynamics and ecosystem services were not addressed.
